instruction: Design the main screen (a single page) for a grid-based puzzle game about pushing boxes and pulling levers. Include: a title and HUD (level, moves), and the puzzle board with the player, one or more crates, a lever, a target/goal (and a door), walls, and a controls legend. Put strong emphasis on the visual design: a distinct identity and a board that reads as a real puzzle — careful layout, color, typography and finish. Make this screen look genuinely beautiful and polished.

history.critique: Brief & Intent: All required elements are present (title, level/moves HUD, worker, crate, lever, target pad, exit door, walls, controls legend), but the single-screen promise is broken: the viewport clips the exit door and its 'EXIT' label at the bottom edge and cuts off the on-screen D-pad, so a required element is only partially visible and the page reads as a scroll, not a main screen. The target pad's down-arrow glyph contradicts the actual solution (the crate must be pushed UP onto the pad), and the lever renders as a red ball on a stick that reads as a pin/balloon rather than a flippable control. Clarity & Hierarchy: The board is the intended focal point but its interior is a sparse 3x4 field with five entities stacked in one vertical column and large dead floor areas, so the puzzle reads as a list rather than a spatial problem; the flat, low-contrast floor makes grid cells and boundaries muddy. The legend icons are abstract glyphs (red slash for lever, dot-square for door) that do not match the actual board sprites, weakening the legend's job. The 'par 8 ✓' checkmark next to 0 moves is a state-logic error, and the board header objective line duplicates the Objectives panel. Visual System & Craft: The amber/gold/teal/red palette and two-tone serif title are cohesive and the crate, worker, and door are well-modeled, but the floor is a flat single tone with faint grid lines, the board frame is thin, and the wall hatching is flat, so the board lacks the depth/finish the brief demands; the clipped door and D-pad are hard jank. Expressiveness & Distinctiveness: The warehouse-amber identity and goggled worker give it character, and the slatted locked door is a genuinely authored moment, but the large empty floor, generic dark-dashboard chrome, and the semantically wrong pad arrow undercut the 'real puzzle' feel; there are no environmental details (floor wear, hazard markings, light) to sell the setting. Key trade-off: fitting everything in one viewport vs. keeping tiles large enough to feel like a real board — currently the design chose richness over fit and lost the door.
history.suggestion: Prioritized plan (all offline, no new assets): 1) Fix viewport fit first — this is the blocking defect. Compress vertical rhythm: make the top HUD a single tighter row (reduce chip padding, drop the sub-labels to one line), trim sidebar panel padding, and scale board tiles down ~10–15% (or reduce the board header strip height) so the full 5x5 board including the door, its 'EXIT' label, and the D-pad render completely with no scroll. 2) Make the board read as a complete puzzle: raise floor/wall contrast (slightly lighter floor, crisp 1px grid lines, subtle inner shadow on the board frame), add a soft radial light pool under the worker, and fill dead space with non-interactive environment detail — faint floor scuffs, a hazard-stripe threshold in front of the door, and a subtle vignette — so the empty cells feel like a warehouse, not blank canvas. 3) Repair semantic clarity: replace the pad's down-arrow with a dashed crate-outline 'goal' glyph (optionally a gold glow when the crate is adjacent), redesign the lever as a base plate with a tilting handle plus a small arc/flip cue so 'flip it' is legible, and re-render the legend icons as exact mini-versions of the board sprites (worker, crate, lever, pad, door, wall) so legend and board match 1:1. 4) Tighten hierarchy and states: unify type (mono for data/labels, one sans for body), remove the redundant board-header objective line in favor of a slim status strip, fix the 'par 8 ✓' logic (show '—' until moves > 0), and visually link the door's lock to the Objectives 'LOCKED' badge (same red, same lock glyph). 5) Preserve and extend expression within the existing system: keep the amber/teal/red palette and two-tone title, add a faint grain/vignette to the board, and define hover/active states (pad glow, lever tilt) so the screen feels alive while remaining a static, self-contained page.

The 'MOVES 0 / seat the crate' chip conflates a counter with an instruction. Clarity & Hierarchy: The five interactive pieces sit at similar visual weight in a large empty tan field, giving the eye no entry point; the dashed target pad is the weakest element on the board and reads as a UI selection box rather than a goal; the lever reads as a lollipop (floating red ball, tilted stick, detached dark pill base) with no up/down state; small mono labels ('The Loading Bay', 'push me', 'flip it', 'solid', 'EXIT') are below comfortable contrast. Visual System & Craft: The most serious jank is that the board overflows the viewport — the bottom wall row and the lower half of the exit door are clipped, breaking the single-screen promise. Legend icons do not match the board entities (flat circle vs. 3D visor ball; flat lever vs. 3D lever), so the system is not one. The floor is a flat uniform tan with no depth, texture, or vignette, so the hatched walls and glossy pieces float on an empty stage. Expressiveness: The amber 'loading bay' identity (hatched walls, gold serif title, mono tags, BAY 07 header) is genuinely distinct and worth keeping, but authored detail stops at the pieces — no floor markings, no hazard treatment on the door, and the cute visor ball is tonally slightly off from the industrial theme.
